newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Ecopetrol begins repairs on Colombian pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Ecopetrol begins repairs on Colombian pipeline.

text.p: Technicians of state-run oil company Ecopetrol began repair work on a dynamite-damaged section of the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline in eastern Colombia Thursday afternoon, a company spokesman said.

The pipeline, which has capacity to pump 250,000 barrels per day, has been out of action since a leftist rebel attack on July 6. An Ecopetrol spokesman estimated repairs would be completed within 48 hours.
"Teams have moved in and are beginning repair work on the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline," the spokesman said. Operations began at about 1500 local time (2000 GMT).
The break was repaired after a first rebel attack on July 6 but was hit less than an hour later by a second rebel blast on July 10 near the town of Arauquita in Arauca province.

It was still unclear whether the pipeline was also ruptured in another section in northeast Norte de Santander province. An Ecopetrol spokesman said repair teams had been unable to gain access to that area around the town of El Carmen because of the presence of National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrillas.
